content_html:
Spirituality: A Double‑Edged Adaptation

Cohesion vs. Conflict

Spiritual concepts increase in‑group cohesion and prosociality, yet can sharpen boundaries and fuel war. This panel maps both sides, mechanisms, and mitigation levers.

Evolutionary Assets (Within‑Group)

Stronger cohesion and trust via shared sacred narratives.

Stabilised cooperation through surveillance by moralising gods and ritual commitments.

Enhanced prosociality in contexts of awe/ritual (helping, generosity).

Resilience under stress: meaning‑making buffers mortality and uncertainty.

Awe → small self

Mechanisms

Sacred values (non‑negotiable) resist trade‑offs → intractable disputes.

Parochial altruism: altruism for insiders + hostility to outsiders.

Identity fusion: self ≈ group; personal cost for group goals rises.

Leadership framing: elites weaponise sacred narratives for mobilisation.

Threat amplification: intergroup anxiety heightens boundary policing.

Evolutionary Liabilities (Between‑Group)

Out‑group conflict and dehumanisation.

War mobilisation via sacralised causes (“holy war”).

Intractability when sacred values collide (“taboo trade‑offs”).

Resource loss & mortality — species‑level risk if escalatory.

Boundary hardening

Cosmic framing

Martyr signals

Why it Persists (Multi‑Level Selection)

Individual: Belief in supernatural monitoring & afterlife can reduce cheating and increase well‑being.

Group: Highly cohesive groups may outcompete rivals (including through conflict), spreading their cultural packages.

Cultural evolution: Memes that bind tightly can transmit reliably, even if costly.

Mitigation Levers

Superordinate goals: shared projects that cross group lines.

Sacred‑value reconciliation: symbolic concessions, value‑respecting reframes (avoid “taboo trade‑offs”).

Ritual redesign: inclusive, interfaith, awe‑inducing practices without threat cues.

Contact + perspective taking: structured cross‑group encounters.
